solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dodgy dealer putting note on Maserati? (9)

indicatorNotes.putting: placing one piece next to another, joining them
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, 'on' puts the note after the car

blocks.note: a Maserati is an example of a car, hence the question mark
D sharp is a musical note

annotation.surface: A shady trader turning up in a flashy Italian sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Maserati stands for any car. A cardsharp cheats at cards, so the dealer is dodgy in the card-table sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a twist: a card cheat deals crooked hands, so 'dealer' is literal at the card table.

entries.clue: Trees mostly concealing Resistance unit (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.concealing: the trees hide the next letter inside them

blocks.note: COPSE (a thicket of trees) without its last letter
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, placed inside COPS

annotation.surface: A wartime Resistance cell hiding out in the woods.
annotation.walkthrough: Resistance with a capital R suggests the French underground, which suits a hidden unit; it is only the physics symbol R.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain military synonym: an army is organised into large formations of two or more divisions, each such formation being a unit.

entries.clue: Irresolute aunts in a dither? It could be fatal (7,8)

indicatorNotes.in a dither: a dither is a state of confusion, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: Two indecisive aunts fretting over a choice that might prove deadly.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: Russian roulette, spinning a revolver's chamber with one bullet loaded, is the game that could be fatal.
annotation.definitionFit: Russian roulette is a deadly gamble, something that could well be fatal.

entries.clue: Good pay includes workers receiving raise (8)

indicatorNotes.includes: the pay holds the next piece inside it
indicatorNotes.raise: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: salary = pay
TU (trade union) = workers, turned up to UT and put inside SAL…ARY

annotation.surface: A decent pay deal in which the workers finally get their rise.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a pay rise, but 'raise' is the reversal instruction for TU in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of beneficial: a lesson that does you good, even if unwelcome.

entries.clue: Article on Europeans welcoming British performers (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the article sits on top of what follows
indicatorNotes.welcoming: the Europeans take the next letter in

blocks.note: the indefinite article
Croats are Europeans, from Croatia
B = British, placed inside CRO…ATS

annotation.surface: A newspaper piece about continental visitors hosting a British troupe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Europeans' is deliberately vague: it has to become one particular nationality, CROATS, to leave room for the B.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: tumblers and trapeze artists are one kind of circus performer.

entries.clue: Insane writer’s written about shock treatment (6)

indicatorNotes.written about: the writer's name is written around the other word

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the writer; 'writer's' = writer is
mad = insane, placed inside PO…E

annotation.surface: A mad author writing about electroconvulsive therapy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shock treatment' reads as psychiatry beside 'insane', but a shock here is a shock of hair, and pomade is the grease that treats it.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a scented hair ointment is something you treat an unruly mop of hair with.

entries.clue: Bill going round church lot (5)

indicatorNotes.going round: turning round, so the bill reads backwards

blocks.note: tab = bill, turned round
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

annotation.surface: A bill being passed around a church congregation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is the tab you run up at a bar, not a law or a bird's beak.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a set of goods sold or made together, as at an auction where each is a lot.

entries.clue: Harmless getting inebriated a little on way north (6)

indicatorNotes.a little: only a small part of the phrase is used
indicatorNotes.on way north: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: the letters run inside gettiNG INEBriated

annotation.surface: Someone getting a bit tipsy on a trip up north, doing no harm.
annotation.walkthrough: The drinking picture hides a reversed run of letters; 'gin' sits in the middle to tempt you towards a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, familiar from medicine, where a growth that is not cancerous does no harm.

entries.clue: Book about coxed pair? (5,3,2,1,4)

blocks.note: the surface suggests a rowing manual; the setter means a novel whose title you need
a coxed pair carries two rowers plus a cox, so the crew counts three, and the title describes exactly that

annotation.surface: A rowing manual about the two-oar boat with a coxswain.
annotation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat is Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel of a Thames boating trip. A coxed pair literally puts three men in a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: Jerome's comic novel is 'about' a crew of three on the Thames, which is what a coxed pair holds.

entries.clue: One’s death possibly memorialised here? (9)

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly be arranged another way

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Where a person's passing gets recorded.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a headstone marks where someone's death is remembered.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue describes the grave marker, which carries the dates of a person's death as a memorial.

entries.clue: One wrongly taking stone imprisoned by His Majesty? (7)

indicatorNotes.imprisoned by: the stone is held inside the ruler

blocks.note: a king is a ruler; the question mark marks the example
st = stone, the unit of weight, placed inside RU…LER

annotation.surface: A thief who took a gem and was locked up by the King.
annotation.walkthrough: A rustler steals livestock, so 'one wrongly taking' fits, though the surface suggests a jewel thief.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: a cattle or horse thief is one who takes animals wrongly.

entries.clue: Island hunter stalking soldiers (7)

indicatorNotes.stalking: the hunter follows behind the soldiers

blocks.note: men = soldiers, as in officers and men
the orca, or killer whale, is a hunter

annotation.surface: A predator on an island tracking a group of troops.
annotation.walkthrough: The hunter is an animal, not a person: ORCA. Menorca is one of Spain's Balearic Islands.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Go round in tutu? (5)

blocks.note: the verb: to pass along the edge of something rather than through it
the noun: a tutu is one type of this garment; the question mark marks the example

annotation.surface: A ballerina twirling in her tutu.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pirouette, but 'Go round' is avoiding something and the tutu is just an example of the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the verb for avoiding by going round the edge, and the garment a ballet tutu is an example of.

entries.clue: Gradually acquire qualifications, you say? (2,7)

indicatorNotes.you say: spoken out loud, the phrase sounds like the answer

blocks.note: buy = acquire, degrees = qualifications

annotation.surface: Someone slowly working through university courses.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is buying degrees rather than earning them.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: progressing a little at a time, one step or grade after another.

entries.clue: Material at one time mainly found in Greek island (8)

indicatorNotes.mainly: most of the word, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.found in: the shortened word sits inside the island

blocks.note: Crete is a Greek island
once = at one time, without its last letter, placed inside C…RETE

annotation.surface: A fabric once made on a Greek island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests cloth; it is building material.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the cement-and-aggregate mix is a building material.

entries.clue: Officer with Italian horses (9)

blocks.note: con is Italian for with
a stable is a set of horses kept together

annotation.surface: A policeman on horseback from Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian' goes with 'with' rather than 'horses': it tells you to put the word into Italian.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the lowest rank of British police officer.

entries.clue: Note motorway sign briefly coming back (4)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.coming back: returning, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
omen = sign, cut to OME, then turned round

annotation.surface: Spotting a motorway sign again on the return journey.
annotation.walkthrough: The sign is an omen, not a road sign, despite the motorway beside it. British motorways are numbered M1, M4 and so on.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: short for memorandum, a brief written note or reminder.

entries.clue: Scripture worthily translated (4,4)

indicatorNotes.translated: turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A sacred text given a faithful translation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Translated' fits Bible translation perfectly, which makes it easy to miss as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the old phrase for sacred writings, especially the Bible.

entries.clue: Ran off with moped, sorry! (6,2)

indicatorNotes.off: gone off, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined to RAN by 'with'

annotation.surface: A thief apologising for riding off on someone's moped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a stolen scooter; 'off' goes with the letters, not the getaway.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrases are polite apologies, interchangeable as exclamations.

entries.clue: Nobody moving east for such bright lights? (4)

annotation.definitionNote: neon is the gas; 'such bright lights' are neon lights

indicatorNotes.moving east: the E (east) moves to a new place in the word

blocks.note: none = nobody; its E shifts from the end to second place

annotation.surface: Nobody heads east to see the bright lights.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves: the E of NONE travels forward, turning NONE into NEON.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the glowing gas-tube signs of city streets are named after the gas inside them.

entries.clue: Poignant dropping leader’s case (8)

indicatorNotes.dropping leader’s: a word's leader is its first letter, and dropping it lets that letter fall away

blocks.note: evocative = poignant, without its first letter E

annotation.surface: A moving story about a leader's fall from office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' is grammatical: the vocative is the case used to address someone, as in Latin.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the grammatical case used when addressing someone directly, as in Latin 'Et tu, Brute'.

entries.clue: Maintain the Speaker’s a sure thing (6)

indicatorNotes.the Speaker’s: as a speaker would say it, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

annotation.surface: The Commons Speaker insisting something is certain.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S points to the Speaker of the House of Commons, but any speaker will do. A cert is British slang for a certainty, often a racing tip.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to state firmly that something is so.

entries.clue: Try to gain favour with commanding officers? Of course (4,2)

blocks.note: CO = commanding officer, so COs are commanding officers
yup = of course, yes

annotation.surface: An ambitious soldier sucking up to the officers, naturally.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition includes 'with': you cosy up to someone to gain favour with them.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to ingratiate yourself by getting friendly with someone.

entries.clue: Spooner saying delay right-winger? It seems unlikely (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Spooner saying: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: stall = delay; it hands its opening S to the next word
Tory = right-winger; it receives the S from STALL

annotation.surface: A claim that a Tory politician is being held up sounds far-fetched.
annotation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party. Moving the S across turns STALL TORY into TALL STORY.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an exaggerated, hard-to-believe tale, so the definition describes it rather than naming it.

entries.clue: Vice-admiral departs Harrow (5)

blocks.note: d = departs, as on a timetable
a harrow is a farm rake for breaking up soil

annotation.surface: A senior naval officer leaving Harrow, the public school.
annotation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the school or the London suburb; it is the farm implement. Sir Francis Drake was vice-admiral against the Armada.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sir Francis held that rank against the Spanish Armada in 1588.

entries.clue: Almost losing knight in advance (5)

indicatorNotes.losing: what you lose is no longer there, so the knight's letter comes out

blocks.note: nearly = almost, losing N (knight in chess notation)

annotation.surface: A chess player close to losing a knight while ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: N is the knight in chess notation, because K is taken by the king.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: arriving before the expected time is arriving ahead of it.

entries.clue: Storeroom, say, involved in case of burglary (7)

indicatorNotes.case of: the outside letters, the case around the word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of burglary
utter = say, placed inside B…Y

annotation.surface: A storeroom involved in a burglary case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' after Storeroom; it is the verb, UTTER. A buttery is a pantry, still the name for a food store in some colleges.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, now old-fashioned: a pantry for provisions, originally where casks (butts) of drink were kept.

entries.clue: Bitterness evident in Tehran courtroom (7)

indicatorNotes.evident in: plainly visible inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run inside TehRAN COURtroom

annotation.surface: Resentment on display in an Iranian court.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is plausible enough to read straight past the letters sitting across the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: long-held resentment, a bitter ill will.

entries.clue: Fire judge in middle of week with court evacuated (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the judge goes inside the middle letters
indicatorNotes.middle of: the central letters of the word
indicatorNotes.evacuated: emptied of its insides, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: the middle two letters of wEEk
J = judge, placed inside E…E
the outer letters of CourT

annotation.surface: A judge firing someone midweek once the court is cleared.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fire' means throw out, as in fire from a job; to eject is to expel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of throw out, as a pilot's seat fires them clear of the plane.

entries.clue: Obviously one boards without trying to push in? (9)

indicatorNotes.boards: gets on board, entering the other word

blocks.note: patently = obviously
I = one, placed inside PAT…ENTLY

annotation.surface: A passenger boarding without jumping the queue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boards' reads as getting on a bus, which suits the queue; it tells I to get into PATENTLY.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: waiting your turn calmly in a queue is the opposite of trying to jump it.
